Bone graft incorporation

Summary of the Evidence

Seven primary publications directly address grafted bone: two human reports on alveolar bone grafting and five animal experiments. One 2026 human publication evaluated local and vascular PBM in different cleft groups at one centre and remains one publication, not two independent trials. A related 2019 systematic review covers earlier, partly overlapping animal work with bovine bone grafts and is counted separately (Dos Santos et al. 2026; Rosso et al. 2019).

Human and clinical evidence

In a controlled study of 87 people with cleft lip and palate, local PBM after alveolar bone grafting produced favorable Chelsea bone-bridge classifications at two months in 80% of participants, compared with 45% after simulated treatment. The separate radial-artery vascular protocol produced 37.5% favorable classifications. The protocols were evaluated in different cleft groups rather than in a direct head-to-head comparison (Dos Santos et al. 2026).

A separate randomized study of 42 patients tested vascular PBM during early postoperative recovery. Facial pain and edema did not differ significantly between groups at 24 hours, while facial temperature variation was lower in the vascular-PBM group. This study assessed postoperative recovery rather than graft incorporation (de Freitas et al. 2025).

Animal evidence

Five animal publications examined rabbit allografts or rat autografts and bovine-bone grafts. Two rat studies reported gains in some bone-formation measures after 660-nm red, 808-nm near-infrared, or combined treatment, but a later implant study did not find significant improvement in bone-to-implant contact or bone between implant threads (Pereira et al. 2025; Pereira et al. 2026).

A rabbit experiment reported graft incorporation, less early inflammation, and greater collagen deposition after 830-nm treatment. An earlier rat experiment reported accelerated integration of an autogenous graft stabilized with fibrin sealant (Valiati et al. 2012; Gonçalves et al. 2016).

One rat study found that a collagen membrane reduced transmission of 808-nm light by 78%. Bone formation was greater when the membrane was not interposed, making this primarily a treatment-delivery finding within an animal experiment (Varela et al. 2023).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No independent cell-culture programme was identified for graft incorporation. The Varela animal publication included a laboratory test of light transmission through a collagen membrane; this component is part of the same publication rather than a separate study (Varela et al. 2023).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The human local protocol used an 880-nm near-infrared laser at 4 J per point over 14 extraoral points immediately after surgery and again at 24 hours. The vascular protocols used 660-nm red light over the radial artery. Animal studies used 660-nm red and 808–830-nm near-infrared light with varied schedules. These studies do not establish a common optimal dose, and their graft materials, anatomical sites, delivery routes, and healing measures differ (Dos Santos et al. 2026; de Freitas et al. 2025).

Interpretation

Local PBM improved one early radiographic bone-bridge classification in a controlled cleft-grafting study, whereas vascular PBM did not improve that graft outcome. Animal experiments report gains in some bone-formation measures but not consistently in implant-integration outcomes. The local clinical finding needs independent replication with standardized graft outcomes and longer follow-up.

Publications and records

8 relevant publications

Seven direct primary publications and one related systematic review.

Clinical effect sizes (estimate)

Favorable Chelsea bone-bridge classifications at two months

Local PBM: 80%

Simulated treatment: 45%

Vascular PBM: 37.5%

The three groups came from different cleft categories within one controlled publication (Dos Santos et al. 2026).

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Low-to-moderate for improved early bone-bridge classification with local PBM after cleft alveolar grafting

The favorable result comes from one controlled 87-patient publication (Dos Santos et al. 2026).

Low for vascular PBM effects on graft incorporation or early recovery

One graft outcome was unfavorable and a separate randomized recovery trial found no clear effect on facial pain or edema (Dos Santos et al. 2026; de Freitas et al. 2025).

Low for osseointegration after grafting in animal models

Bone findings varied by outcome and protocol.

Rationale for the certainty assessment

One controlled 87-patient publication reported more favorable early bone-bridge ratings after local near-infrared PBM but not after its separate vascular protocol. A 42-patient randomized trial of vascular PBM found no clear improvement in facial pain or edema. Animal studies report gains in some bone measures but null implant-contact outcomes. Confidence is limited by single-centre clinical evidence, short follow-up, and varied grafts and protocols (Dos Santos et al. 2026; de Freitas et al. 2025).
